6 Best Web Scraping Tools for Reliable Data Extraction (2026)

The best web scraping tools in 2026 are Apify for its marketplace of pre-built scrapers, Bright Data for sites that actively block scrapers, Browse AI and Octoparse for no-code scraping, ScrapingBee for a developer API, and Diffbot for AI-structured extraction. Five of the six have a free plan, and ScrapingBee has a free trial (see the free tiers section below).

A web scraping tool that works in a demo and a web scraping tool that survives a site redesign three months from now are not the same purchase. The gap between them is what happens when a target site changes its markup, adds a CAPTCHA, or rate-limits your IP, not which tool extracted a clean table on the first try. This guide compares 6 real web scraping platforms on verified G2 reviews, published pricing, and what each one is actually built for, so you know which one survives contact with a real target site.

Disclosure: every G2 rating and review count below was first pulled on September 8, 2026 and re-checked on October 21, 2026, cross-checked against each vendor's own pricing page for every dollar figure cited.
Last checked: October 2026 (pricing and features re-verified).
How we compared these tools

Four criteria: (1) Verified reputation: real G2 reviews, not a vendor's own testimonials page. (2) Pricing transparency: a published rate card, not "contact us" as the only answer. (3) No-code vs. developer-first: does the tool assume a visual point-and-click workflow, or an API a developer calls from code? (4) What breaks it: JavaScript-heavy sites, anti-bot measures, and site-layout changes are where scraping tools actually differ, not the marketing page.

1. Apify, best for the largest actor marketplace and AI-agent integration

Apify runs on a marketplace model: instead of building every scraper from scratch, its "Actors" store offers thousands of pre-built, maintained scrapers for common targets (ecommerce sites, social platforms, business registries) that run on Apify's own cloud infrastructure. Its G2 profile shows 676 reviews at 4.7/5 (October 2026), the largest review count of any tool on this list by a wide margin. A recent addition, an MCP server, lets an AI agent call Apify actors as a tool, pulling live web data directly into an agent's context.
Best for: teams that want to skip building and maintaining their own scrapers for common targets, and teams building AI agents that need live web data as a callable tool.
Pricing: Free tier includes $5 of monthly usage; Starter $19/mo; Scale $199/mo; Business $999/mo; compute billed per CU ($0.13-$0.20 depending on tier) on top of the included allowance.

Pros: by far the largest verified review base on this list; actor marketplace means many common scraping targets are already solved; MCP server is a genuine, distinctive integration for AI-agent workflows other tools on this list don't offer.

Cons: usage-based compute pricing is hard to estimate before a run finishes, per multiple G2 reviews citing unexpected cost on misconfigured jobs; marketplace actor quality varies since anyone can publish one, and a popular actor can break after an update with no clear signal of how recently it was maintained.
2. Bright Data, best for enterprise-scale anti-blocking infrastructure

Bright Data is built around proxy infrastructure (residential, datacenter, and mobile IPs) combined with a Web Scraper API that handles JavaScript rendering, CAPTCHA solving, and geotargeting. Its G2 profile shows 348 reviews at 4.7/5 (October 2026), the second-largest review base on this list.
Best for: teams scraping targets that actively fight back with IP blocking, CAPTCHAs, or geo-restrictions at meaningful volume.
Pricing: Free tier includes 5,000 records/month; pay-as-you-go at $1.50 per 1,000 records; Scale plan $499/mo for 384,000 records/month ($1.30 per additional 1,000); Enterprise custom.

Pros: proxy and anti-blocking infrastructure built specifically for hostile targets, not bolted on; unlimited concurrency on every paid tier; identical core feature set (JS rendering, CAPTCHA solving, data validation) across all tiers rather than gating features by price.

Cons: per-record pricing can get expensive at very high volume compared to Apify's compute-based model for lighter workloads; the breadth of Bright Data's product line (proxies, SERP API, Scraping Browser, Web Unlocker) means picking the right specific product takes more upfront research than a single-product competitor.
3. Browse AI, best for no-code robot training and change monitoring

Browse AI uses a point-and-click "robot" trainer: you demonstrate the extraction once on a real page, and the robot repeats it on a schedule, with alerts when the tracked data changes. Its G2 profile shows 61 verified reviews at 4.8/5.
Best for: non-developers who need to monitor a specific set of pages for changes (price tracking, competitor monitoring, lead lists) without writing code.
Pricing: Free tier with 50 credits/month, 2 websites; Personal from $19/mo (billed annually); Professional from $69/mo; Premium from $500/mo with a dedicated account manager.

Pros: genuinely no-code, trained by demonstration rather than configuration; built-in change monitoring and alerting is a first-class feature, not an add-on; unlimited robots on every plan, including free.
Cons: credit-based limits mean heavier monitoring schedules need a higher tier quickly; smaller review base than Apify or Bright Data, though still a healthy sample at 61.
4. Octoparse, best for a mature no-code visual workflow with cloud scheduling

Octoparse offers a visual point-and-click workflow designer with both local (desktop) and cloud extraction, 500+ preset templates for common sites, and built-in IP rotation and CAPTCHA solving on paid tiers. Its G2 profile shows 52 verified reviews at 4.8/5.
Best for: teams that want a no-code visual builder with more workflow control (branching logic, scheduling, multiple concurrent cloud processes) than a simpler point-and-click tool offers.

Pricing: Free tier with 10 tasks and 50,000 rows/month; Standard from $69/mo (100 tasks, 3 concurrent cloud processes); Professional $249/mo (250 tasks, 20 concurrent processes, priority support); Enterprise custom.

Pros: 500+ preset templates cover common extraction targets out of the box; cloud task monitoring and storage integrations (Google Sheets, Dropbox, S3) are included at the Professional tier; a 30% startup discount program is a real, published offer, not a negotiated exception.

Cons: the free tier's 50,000-row export cap is restrictive for anything beyond light testing; Professional-tier pricing ($249/mo) sits above Browse AI's comparable tier for a similar no-code audience.
5. ScrapingBee, best for a developer-first scraping API

ScrapingBee is a single API endpoint that handles headless Chrome rendering, proxy rotation, and CAPTCHA avoidance behind one call, aimed at developers who want to write their own scraping logic without managing browser infrastructure themselves. Its G2 profile shows 33 reviews at 4.8/5 (October 2026).
Best for: developers who want to keep scraping logic in their own codebase and just need the browser-and-proxy infrastructure handled for them, rather than a full no-code platform.

Pricing: Hobby $19/mo (75,000 API credits, 25 concurrent requests); Freelance $49/mo; Startup $99/mo; Business $249/mo; Business+ $599/mo (8,000,000 credits, 400 concurrent requests); free trial with 1,000 API credits, no credit card required.

Pros: simplest integration model on this list for a developer who already has scraping logic and just needs infrastructure; concurrency scales cleanly with plan tier; a no-credit-card free trial for testing before committing.
Cons: second-smallest review base on this list (33 reviews); no visual workflow builder or no-code option, so it's the wrong fit for a non-developer team.
6. Diffbot, best for AI-structured extraction and Knowledge Graph data

Diffbot takes a different approach from the rest of this list: instead of returning raw HTML or a scraped table, its APIs use machine learning to identify and return structured data (article text, product details, entities) directly from a page, plus access to its own Knowledge Graph of pre-extracted entities. Its G2 profile shows 29 verified reviews at 4.9/5, the highest rating on this list.
Best for: teams that need structured, semantic data (articles, products, organizations, people) rather than raw scraped HTML they'd otherwise have to parse themselves.

Pricing: Free tier with 10,000 credits/month, all four APIs included; Startup $299/mo (250,000 credits, overage at $0.001/credit); Plus $899/mo (1,000,000 credits, Crawl access, 3 seats); Enterprise custom.

Pros: highest G2 rating on this list; structured extraction (article, product, entity) removes a parsing step every other tool on this list still leaves to you; Knowledge Graph access is a genuinely distinctive feature no other entry here offers.

Cons: starting price ($299/mo for the first paid tier) is the highest entry point on this list after Bright Data's Scale plan; smallest review base on this list (29 reviews), though its 4.9/5 rating is the strongest of any tool here.

Free web scraping tools: what each free tier includes

If you are looking for the best web scraping tools free of charge, five of the six tools above have a permanent free plan and ScrapingBee has a free trial. Here is what each one gives you, from each vendor's pricing page on October 21, 2026.

For a one-off job, start with the free plan that matches how you work: Browse AI or Octoparse if you want no-code, Apify if a pre-built Actor already covers your target site, Diffbot if you need structured article or product data. Open-source libraries such as Scrapy, Playwright and Beautiful Soup cost nothing to use, but you run the code, the browsers and the proxies yourself.
When a scraping tool is the wrong call

Every tool above assumes someone on your team can configure, test, and maintain the extraction logic, whether that's a no-code robot or a developer-written API call. If that capacity doesn't exist, or the pipeline needs to feed directly into your own CRM, database, or an AI agent's decision logic rather than a spreadsheet export, the honest options are building it in-house or working with a partner that builds and maintains it for you. Red flags when evaluating a web scraping tool
No published starting price anywhere, not even a wide range, before a sales call.
A vendor demo that only shows a simple, static HTML page. Ask specifically how the tool handles a JavaScript-heavy site, a login wall, or a CAPTCHA, since that's where most tools actually differ.
Usage-based pricing with no cost estimate shown before a run executes. Ask directly how the tool prevents a misconfigured job from draining your budget overnight.
No visibility into how recently a pre-built template or actor was last updated, on marketplace-model tools. A scraper built for last year's site layout can silently return empty or wrong data.

No mention of legal or terms-of-service considerations for the specific sites you plan to scrape. Scraping tools handle the technical extraction; they don't make a site's terms of service or applicable law disappear.
FAQ
What is a web scraping tool?

A web scraping tool extracts structured data from web pages automatically, rather than requiring someone to manually copy and paste information. Tools on this list range from no-code point-and-click platforms (Browse AI, Octoparse) to developer-first APIs (ScrapingBee, Diffbot) to infrastructure platforms built around proxy networks (Bright Data) and marketplace models (Apify).
Is web scraping legal?

It depends on what's being scraped and how. Publicly accessible data generally carries less legal risk than data behind a login wall, and a target site's own terms of service can restrict scraping even when the data is public. This is a legal question specific to your situation and the sites you plan to target, not something any tool on this list resolves for you; consult counsel for anything beyond casual, low-volume use.
What are the best free web scraping tools?

Apify, Bright Data, Browse AI, Octoparse and Diffbot all have a free plan, and ScrapingBee has a 1,000-credit free trial. Apify gives $5 of usage a month, Bright Data 5,000 records, Browse AI 50 credits, Octoparse 10 tasks and 50,000 rows, and Diffbot 10,000 credits (vendor pricing pages, October 2026).
What's the difference between a no-code scraping tool and a scraping API?

A no-code tool (Browse AI, Octoparse) gives you a visual interface to configure extraction without writing code, aimed at non-developers. A scraping API (ScrapingBee, Diffbot) is a service you call from your own code, aimed at developers who want to keep the scraping logic in their own codebase and just need infrastructure (browser rendering, proxies) handled.
How much does a web scraping tool cost?

Entry-level tools on this list start free or under $20/month for light use (ScrapingBee, Browse AI, Apify's Starter tier). Mid-volume, business-grade use typically runs $69-249/month depending on the tool and volume. Enterprise-scale extraction, especially against sites with active anti-bot defenses, can run $500-1,000+/month or move to custom Enterprise pricing.
Can a scraping tool handle JavaScript-heavy websites?

Most tools on this list handle JavaScript rendering (headless Chrome or equivalent) on at least their paid tiers, including ScrapingBee, Bright Data, Apify, and Octoparse. Confirm this specifically for your target sites before committing, since rendering-heavy pages are one of the most common places a scraping tool fails in practice, not in the sales demo.
What happens when a target website changes its layout?

Every tool on this list can break when a target site changes its markup, since extraction logic is typically built against a specific page structure. The real differentiator is how quickly you find out: Apify and Browse AI both surface run failures and alerts rather than silently returning empty data, which several G2 reviews specifically credit as valuable versus discovering a dead pipeline days later.
The tool is not the hard part

Every platform on this list can technically extract the data you have in mind from a target page. The actual constraint is almost always what happens after extraction, feeding that data reliably into your CRM, your database, or an agent's decision logic, and what happens when the target site changes, not which tool's demo looked cleanest.
